summary.text: The Corinthian brigand — son of Pelops, or in some accounts of Poseidon — who held the Scironian rocks on the Megarian side of the Isthmus and forced passers-by to wash his feet before kicking them into the sea for a tortoise to devour, until Theseus cast him down by the same death.

Distinct from Sciron father of Endeïs, grandfather of Peleus and Telamon on Aegina (`Bibliotheca 3.12.6`), and from the Megarian war-minister Sciron of Athenian royal genealogy in Pausanias — this is the Isthmus robber of the Theseus road.

story.text: In the Megarian territory Sciron held the rocks called Scironian after him. He made travellers wash his feet and, in the act of washing, kicked them into the deep where a huge turtle preyed on them. Theseus seized him by the feet and threw him into the sea; from this the cliffs kept his name, and Pausanias says the Molurian dock beside them was accursed because Sciron dwelt there.
story.citation: Epitome 1.2; Fabulae 38; Description of Greece 1.44.8; Metamorphoses 7.445–447
